about: A display presents one agent’s published output as a tile and a full canvas. Blocks bind to fields of that output; the tile and figure read the same value.

tile.reads: The output's value, state and needs. The label, the mark and the number format come from the presentation. The label and the unit are held to what a tile draws on one line beside its mark. A mark whose binding the output leaves unfilled rests on the tile, and the display's canvas says what it needs.

ring.needs: Needs a share of a whole.

arc.needs: Needs a share of a whole.

count.reads: A number, written with at most one decimal. The unit is the presentation's own word, or the one the output publishes when it is as short.

money.reads: An amount in the output’s currency.

duration.reads: Seconds, written as seconds under a minute and as minutes and seconds from there.

rate.reads: A percentage. A value above 1, or a value published with the unit %, is the percentage itself: 86.5 reads 86.5 %. Any other value from 0 to 1 is a ratio: 0.865 reads 86.5 %.

figure.draws: The number, as the tile writes it, with its unit and its period.

period.draws: The Weekly, Monthly and Annual switch.
period.needs: Needs a reading for the week, the month and the year.

line.draws: A line over the period. A point opens its instances.

bars.draws: One bar for each band under the block's own title, the tallest lit.
bars.needs: Needs a value for each named band.

gauge.draws: A ring or an arc filled to a share.
gauge.needs: Needs a share of a whole.

key_points.draws: Up to five short points in a panel.
key_points.needs: Needs one to five short points.

recommendation.draws: One recommendation beside an accent rule.

facts.draws: When the owning agent last updated the display, its cadence and its source.
facts.needs: Needs the owning agent and its last update.

instances.draws: A scrolling list of instances, each with its sentence and its time. A row of the output's own rows carries its picture.

timeline.draws: A feed of timed events, newest first, with a comment between them where the output carries comments.

shapes.texts: A list of up to 5 strings.
shapes.points: A list of 2 or more {t, value}: t is an ISO time, value is a number.
shapes.bands: A list of 1 to 12 {label, value}: label (or band) is a string, value is a number.
shapes.rows: A list of {id, at, description}: label may stand for description. The host admits trusted rows; other lists carry text, numbers and times.
shapes.timed_rows: Rows where every at is an ISO time.
shapes.comments: A list of {text}: at (or written_at) places it among the events; id and recommendation are optional. The text slots a display's agent writes fit.
shapes.readings: The same output over the week, the month and the year, as the display’s passes store them.
